body:
## Symptom

Passing a formal component instance directly as SplitPane `start` / `end` breaks that component's own element ref. In oh-my-byted (0.1.7) a panel cell component declares `element_ref("cell_root")` on its root and reads it when the user floats the cell. Once the cell is passed straight into SplitPane, that fails with:

```
component /View[...]/Cell[cell-clock] has no mounted element ref `cell_root`
```

## Cause

`registry/components/split_pane.rhai` (unchanged on `codex/interaction-runtime-0.1.8`) decorates the caller's node in place:

```rhai
let start = props.start.with_key(start_ref_key)                     // :123
    .with_style(ctx.component_style("start", start_style))
    .with_ref(start_ref)                                             // :125
    .bind_signal(if horizontal { "width_override" } else { "height_override" }, preview);
...
let end = props.end.with_key(props.end_key)                         // :152
```

The collapsed paths (:99, :104) do the same with key and style. A node carries one ref, so the component's root ref is replaced, and its key is rewritten as well.

`Draggable` follows the same pattern for `handle` (`props.handle.with_key(..).with_ref(handle_ref)`); not reproduced there. `Resizable` already wraps `content` in its own `box([...])`.

## Workaround

Wrap each pane before passing it: `start: box([node])`.

## Ask

Have SplitPane (and Draggable's `handle`) wrap the caller's node internally, so the component's key / style / ref / signal land on its own wrapper. Callers cannot tell from the outside that their node will be taken over. Alternatively, document it in the component header.

Suggested target: 0.1.9.
title: SplitPane overwrites key/style/ref on the caller's start/end nodes, breaking formal components passed as panes
